timeit.method: Three smaller cases use 31 alternating samples; two controls use 192 balanced randomized rounds and simultaneous block-bootstrap bounds. Three warmups per arm, fixed CPUs recorded per case, parent/default and option-off/default comparisons.

plan.reason: Repeated physical-core monitoring found no sustained quiet interval; prior noisy results are retained and not reused for this inference.
plan.method: 192 balanced randomized three-arm rounds; all six permutations per six-round block, independently shuffled. Moving interference is handled by resampling complete six-round blocks; CPU affinity is fixed within the run.
plan.acceptance: Every original ratio-of-medians CPU/wall comparison AND every upper confidence bound on the ratio of mean CPU/wall times must be <= 5%. All complete results retained; no automatic retry on failure.
plan.cpu_selection: Highest minimum sibling idle percentage over five seconds among allowed physical cores; no idle threshold. No owned builds/tests/scans allowed during measurement.

cases.confidence_method: Percentile bootstrap of 32 complete six-round blocks; simultaneous family alpha 0.05 across eight CPU/wall comparisons.

limitations: Stable Rust 1.93.0/1.93.1 little-endian 64-bit fmt layout only; executed native producer is 1.93.1.
Only exact panic_fmt identities, constant mapped nonvolatile caller-location addresses and supported literal/integer templates qualify.
Recovered source supplies its own panic location and backtrace; original location fields are not reproduced.
Primitive execution uses unchanged macro expressions with explicit typed input bindings; complete descriptor setup is retained and is not universally recompilable.
Full angr Go/Rust parity is not established by this change.
